findings.title: argon2i_32 does not enforce the nb_blocks >= 8*nb_lanes contract, causing heap out-of-bounds write/read for small block counts
findings.evidence: The public function argon2i_32 (line 322) accepts nb_blocks and passes it unvalidated into config.nb_blocks (line 328) and into malloc((size_t)nb_blocks * 1024) (line 345) before calling crypto_argon2 at line 347. Unlike password/salt/key/ad sizes, which are range-checked by _validate_u32 (lines 334-342), nb_blocks has no lower-bound check. Because argon2i_32 hardcodes config.nb_lanes = 1 (line 330), monocypher.c:752-754 computes segment_size = nb_blocks/4 and lane_size = segment_size*4, so for any nb_blocks in {0,1,2,3} both segment_size and lane_size become 0. crypto_argon2 then unconditionally fills two 1024-byte blocks per lane at monocypher.c:776-781 (blocks[l*lane_size + i], i=0,1), so nb_blocks=1 writes a full 1024-byte block at offset 1024, one block past the 1 KiB heap allocation, and nb_blocks=0 writes past a malloc(0) region: an attacker-influenced heap buffer overflow. The same zero lane_size also makes monocypher.c:902 compute last_block = blocks + lane_size - 1 = blocks - 1 and then read last_block->a (1024 bytes) at monocypher.c:911, a large out-of-bounds read whose contents are hashed into the returned key for nb_blocks in {0,1,2,3}. monocypher.h:160 documents the contract 'nb_blocks >= 8 * nb_lanes', but neither the Python wrapper nor the C function enforces it, so a caller that supplies a small Argon2 memory parameter (e.g. argon2i_32(1, 3, password, salt)) reaches the unsafe operations directly.
